• The compressed inverted index is the most space efficient and the fastest data structure for all three operations (Boolean queries, phrase queries and document reporting) for real world (non-regular language) texts.

1) a carefully choreographed use of data compression and indexing can lead to very efficient in-memory text search engines; 2) for natural language texts, compressed inverted indexes are more efficient than suffix arrays for all the three operations: Boolean queries, phrase search, and document retrieval; 3) the compressed indexes are also more compact than the suffix array representations of the text; and 4) the compressed indexes can be used for efficient approximate string matching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a full text index that is both compact and fast.
the development of an efficient full text database for in-memory search engines.
the design and implementation of a full text database that is able to answer queries in a fraction of the time needed by existing systems, using less memory and disk space than the input document.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inverted index is the best data structure for text search.
our data structures are the best in class for the tasks at hand.
our data structure is a good candidate to be a core data structure for in-memory full text search engines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our system uses 1/3 of the space of the input text and is able to answer all queries in less than a second.
our data structure is the first to provide a full text index for real world (English) texts that is faster than the uncompressed suffix array based techniques, and that uses less space than the text.
we present the first in-memory search engine for natural language text that is competitive in terms of speed and storage requirements to the state-of-the-art disk-based search engines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classical data compression techniques can be combined in a very effective manner with search data structures to achieve high compression rates and good search performance.
the inverted index is a surprisingly robust and versatile data structure.
the inverted index is a very powerful data structure that is not just useful for full text retrieval, but can also be used to compress text data in a way that allows for efficient retrieval.
